title: Probing Intersectional Biases in Vision-Language Models with Counterfactual Examples
findings: The evaluated Vision-Language Models (ALIP, CLIP, SLIP) were found to exhibit intersectional biases related to religion and gender across various occupations (e.g., 'Librarian', 'Bartender') and personality traits (e.g., 'Emotional', 'Dogmatic'). The degree and nature of this bias varied between the models.
references: Abeba Birhane, Vinay Uday Prabhu, and Emmanuel Kahembwe. Multimodal datasets: misogyny, pornography, and malignant stereotypes. arXiv preprint arXiv:2110.01963, 2021.
